title: カイロ近郊で燃料タンカー炎上、30人死亡

sources.headline: Egyptian authorities arrest motorist over tanker crash that killed 31
sources.text: Egyptian authorities have arrested a man accused of causing a tanker crash and massive fire that killed 31 people on a busy Cairo highway.The public prosecutor's office said the motorist had confessed to driving at 110km/h (68mph) along a section of ring road, to the north of the old city centre, and clipping the tanker with the side of his car as he changed lanes.Sources close to the investigation were earlier quoted by state media as saying a high-voltage cable had fallen in front of the fuel truck, causing the driver to lose control.Twenty-one others were injured in the crash in the Warraq neighbourhood on Wednesday evening, with hospitals treating patients for burns and smoke inhalation.The public prosecutor's office said on Thursday that "upon questioning the suspect and confronting him with the findings of the investigation... he confessed to committing the act"."He added that, while moving between traffic lanes and overtaking vehicles, the left side of his car collided with the right rear side of the tanker. This caused him to lose control of the steering wheel and his car veered to the far right of the road."At the same time, one of the fuel tanker's tyres burst, causing it to veer into the highway's central reservation, hit the concrete barrier and overturn, spilling fuel and igniting a fire, the prosecutor's office said.Egyptian authorities have not named the suspect accused of causing the fatal crash, but they said he had been travelling with his father at the time.

sources.headline: Road Fire Near Cairo Kills Dozens After Petroleum-Laden Truck Crashes
Driver of car suspected of causing fuel tanker to overturn in Egypt detained
sources.text: The driver of a car suspected to have caused a fuel tanker to overturn in Egypt, causing the deaths of 31 people, has been detained.

sources.headline: Fuel tanker explosion kills 31 on Egyptian highway
sources.text:
By
Ahmed Shawkat
Producer
Ahmed Shawkat is a CBS News producer based in Cairo. He has worked for CBS News since 2016, prior to which he worked with several European networks including TVE, ZDF, SVT and Yle.
Read Full Bio
November 26, 2026 / 6:27 AM EST
/ CBS News
Add CBS News on Google
Cairo — A massive fire on an Egyptian highway killed 31 people and injured 21 others after a car slammed into a fuel tanker truck at high speed, Egypt's Public Prosecution office said Thursday.The driver has been arrested, according to the statement. At least 27 vehicles, including cars and motorcycles, were destroyed in the fire.The prosecutor said the suspect admitted causing the accident while driving around 70 miles per hour on a major highway in the Al-Warraq district of Giza, which is part of the Greater Cairo area.
A fire burns at the site where a vehicle carrying petroleum products overturned and caught fire on a major ring road in Al-Warraq district of Giza, Egypt, Nov. 25, 2026, in a screengrab obtained from social media video.
Habiba Abd El Aziz/REUTERS
The driver said he was changing lanes and overtaking vehicles when the front-left side of his car struck the rear-right side of the tanker, according to the prosecutor's statement, "causing the steering wheel to slip from his hands and his car to veer off course."When the car hit the truck, one of the truck's tires exploded, causing it to overturn and slam into a concrete barrier.Gasoline then leaked from the tanker and caught on fire. Images of the blaze on social media showed multiple vehicles on fire as flames and smoke billowed into the night sky.The prosecutor said the suspect was being questioned to establish the circumstances of the accident and assess any criminal responsibility.
"It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire," Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic behind the accident, told The Associated Press. "It was a shocking scene."Sameer told the AP he saw at least eight bodies being removed from charred vehicles.Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sisi expressed his condolences to the victims of the crash. In a statement on X, Egypt's health ministry said 39 ambulances took part in the rescue operation.
While fatal traffic accidents are common in Egypt, the sheer scale of the incident has prompted calls for greater accountability. Last year, nearly 6,000 people died in road traffic accidents across Egypt, according to official data.

sources.headline: Egyptians mourn, demand accountability after deadly tanker explosion kills 31
sources.text: CAIRO - Egyptian lawmakers demanded accountability on Nov 26 as shocked Cairo residents mourned the deaths of 31 people in an overnight tanker explosion, the deadliest of a series of recent accidents that have stoked public anger.The accident was caused when a car hit the back of the tanker, causing it to overturn and catch fire, public prosecutors said, adding that a suspect has been arrested.“The tanks were exploding, the tyres were exploding, and there was fire,” said local resident Zaghlol al-Me, who arrived at the scene shortly after the accident, but was unable to help anyone due to the intensity of the blaze. “We just didn’t know what to do or how to save anyone.”It was the latest in a string of transport-related accidents, coming less than three weeks after a train collision killed seven people.The government, which has poured billions into new highways, bridges and other infrastructure, needs to move from “building roads and expanding them to managing their safety professionally,” said lawmaker Mahmoud Samy.The Cabinet holds full responsibility and must resign, said Abdel Moneim Imam, a lawmaker and chairman of the liberal Justice Party.Shereen Reda, one of Egypt’s best-known contemporary actresses, said in a post on X that it was time “to ask questions and hold people to account”.Ash and burned tyresTraffic moved slowly amid ash and the remnants of burned tyres along a stretch of the capital’s ring road where the blast took place, as a passersby nervously eyed a pair of oil-product tankers rolling past.Radio stations played patriotic songs while the minister of religious endowments asked Friday sermons to address solidarity in times of crisis.Relatives posted appeals on Facebook for men who had been on the road and had been missing since, including fathers and husbands.Egypt recorded 5,829 road deaths in 2025, up 10.8% from the previous year but down from 7,326 in 2021, according to the official statistics agency, CAPMAS.The transport ministry, which extended condolences to the victims’ families, declined to comment further when contacted by Reuters.String of accidents amid transport investmentTransport Minister Kamel al-Wazir was appointed in 2019 after an earlier transport disaster, when a train crashed at Cairo’s Ramses station, triggering a fire that killed 25 people and prompted his predecessor to resign.His ministry has overseen an ambitious overhaul of the country’s infrastructure, including a monorail to the New Capital east of Cairo and a roughly 2,000km high-speed rail network.Wazir has pointed to individual errors after previous incidents. He rejected calls to resign after a lorry hit a minibus on a highway in the Nile Delta, killing 19 people, almost all of them young women, in July 2025.Amr Moussa, a former foreign minister and Arab League secretary-general, said there had been a “grave deterioration in the system of oversight and follow-up.”“Trading accusations and evading responsibility leads to the next disaster,” he said. REUTERS

sources.headline: Dozens killed in Egypt vehicle fire
At least 30 killed in highway fire in Cairo district
sources.text:
Published on 25 November 2026 - 20:56 GMT+1,Updated
26 November 2026 - 8:18 GMT+1
At least 30 people were killed and 15 others injured after a fire broke out on a major highway in the Egyptian capital Cairo on Wednesday, the country's Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said.
The blaze erupted after a truck carrying fuel overturned on a busy highway, according to Egyptian state media.
Footage captured by passers-by showed a massive blaze and thick clouds of smoke rising from the scene.
Emergency workers pulled people from burning vehicles as firefighters battled the flames. Hundreds of people gathered near the scene in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a suburb of Cairo.
Abdel Ghaffar said 39 ambulances were dispatched to the scene, with 15 injured people taken to hospital.
Egyptian President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi expressed his condolences to the victims in a statement.
The Health Minister said he would visit the scene, adding that the death toll was preliminary and could rise further.
Traffic accidents claim thousands of lives in Egypt every year, with speeding, poor road conditions and inadequate enforcement of traffic laws among the leading causes of crashes.
In January, 21 people were killed and 16 others injured in a multi-vehicle collision on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.
Additional sources • AFP, AP

sources.headline: Fuel tanker crash on major Cairo highway kills at least 30
sources.text: Topic:Accidents and Emergency IncidentsPosted Thu 26 Nov 2026 at 8:04amThu 26 Nov 2026 at 8:04amA crash involving a fuel tanker on a major Cairo highway has killed at least 30 people, authorities say. (AP: Mohammed Salah)In short:A crash involving a fuel tanker on a major Cairo highway has killed at least 30 people, Egyptian authorities say.The blaze also injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred.The public prosecutor’s office says efforts to identify the victims are underway.A fuel tanker crash ignited a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo on Wednesday and killed at least 30 people, according to Egyptian authorities.The blaze on Ring Road, a key artery that encircles the Egyptian capital, injured at least 25 people and left more than two dozen cars and motorcycles charred, the public prosecutor's office said in a statement.The crash occurred on a stretch of the highway at Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in the Greater Cairo area, according to the health ministry.Rescue workers were seen pulling people out of burning cars and an Associated Press video showed firefighters working to put out the fire spreading among vehicles.Hundreds of people gathered in the aftermath of the Cairo crash. (AP: Mohammed Salah)Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi has issued a statement expressing his condolences and the public prosecutor’s office says DNA investigations are underway to identify the victims.Health Minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured were taken to nearby hospitals and that he would head to the scene himself.He said the death toll was preliminary.Deadly traffic accidents claim thousands of lives every year in Egypt, which has a poor transport safety record.Speeding, bad roads and poor enforcement of traffic laws are the main reasons behind most of the crashes.In January 21 people were killed and 16 injured in a massive multi car pile-up on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.AP

sources.headline: Egypt highway inferno kills 30 after fuel tanker overturns
sources.text: Firefighters extinguish fires involving a vehicle carrying petroleum products on the Ring Road in Al-Warraq, in Giza, Cairo, Egypt, Wednesday, Nov. 25. (AP Photo)At least 31 people were killed and 21 injured after a crash involving a fuel tanker triggered a massive fire on a major highway surrounding Cairo in Egypt on Wednesday, authorities said. The blaze broke out on the Ring Road in Waraq, a densely populated neighbourhood in Giza, part of the Greater Cairo region. More than two dozen cars and motorcycles were charred in the fire.The fire spread among vehicles following the crash, trapping people inside burning cars. Rescue workers were seen pulling victims out of the vehicles as firefighters worked to bring the blaze under control, according to an Associated Press video. Hundreds of people gathered near the accident site in the Warraq district of Imbaba, a Cairo suburb.Ahmed Sameer, who was stuck in traffic after the road was blocked, said he saw the fuel tanker and several cars engulfed in flames. He also witnessed at least eight bodies being removed from burned vehicles.“It was a huge fire, the cars got stuck together because of the fire," Associated Press reported quoting him as he described the fear and panic that followed, "It was a shocking scene.”Egyptian President Abdel-Fattah el-Sissi expressed his condolences to the victims. The Public Prosecutor’s office said DNA investigations were underway to identify those killed.Egypt health minister Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the injured had been taken to nearby hospitals. He also said he would visit the accident site. The death toll was preliminary and could rise further, he added.The Ring Road is a major transport artery connecting key highways across Greater Cairo and linking the governorates of Cairo, Giza and Qalyubia.Road accidents are common in Egypt due to factors such as speeding, poor road conditions and weak enforcement of traffic regulations. Thousands of people die in traffic accidents across the country every year.In January, 21 people were killed and 16 injured in a massive multi-vehicle pile-up on a road near the southern province of Beni Suef.
